newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Danish central bank wants narrow bands crown - Euro.
newsitem.headline: Danish central bank wants narrow bands crown - Euro.

text.p: Denmark wants a relationship with narrow fluctuation bands between the crown and the planned European single currency, Central Bank director Jens Thomsen said on Thursday.
"Some sort of narrow bands relationship," Thomsen told Reuters when asked what kind of relationship Denmark wanted to establish with the Euro, due to be introduced in 1999.
Denmark has decided not to join European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU). A referendum would be needed to overturn that decision.

Thomsen, speaking during a seminar on the EMU in Brussels, did not specify how narrow he wanted the crown's bands to be. But he said they should be less than the 15 percent bands in the Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM).
"It is well known we always supported the old system," he said, referring to the way the ERM worked before the currency turmoil of 1993. At that time most currencies traded within 2.25 percent bands.
